exposure: fetal access sites for intrauterine transfusion (intrahepatic, placental insertion, free loop)
outcome: postnatal treatment (intensive phototherapy, exchange transfusion, red blood cell transfusions)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 2420 pregnancies with moderate or severe haemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn from 31 centres in 22 countries, including cases with fetal death at 16+0 weeks or later, those treated antenatally, or neonates receiving intensive postnatal treatment.
finding: The study found considerable variation in antenatal management and outcomes for haemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn across different international sites, with intrahepatic approaches for intrauterine transfusions having lower non-lethal complication rates compared to placental insertion or free loop.
gest_age: Median gestational age at birth for neonates with antenatal treatment was 35.6 weeks, and 37.3 weeks for those without antenatal treatment.
